items.t: North Arm is the GVR board sub-area named for the North Arm of the Fraser River: the river's north-arm foreshore along the south side of mainland New Westminster, below the Marine Way / Stewardson Way corridor, with the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) trail on the foreshore, named in the City's OCP Green Zone list. Precise boundary roads: UNVERIFIED. It is NOT one of the residential neighbourhoods on the City's Official Community Plan residential-neighbourhoods map, and its official City neighbourhood status is UNVERIFIED; the City's statistical planning geography separately uses "North Arm North" and "North Arm South" for industrial areas on the Queensborough / river side, and the board sub-area and the City statistical areas are not confirmed to be the same geography.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere —. This is a foreshore / largely non-residential board geography, not a trading residential neighbourhood.
Parent-community context only: the New Westminster condos & townhomes median was $560,000 in September 2026 ($587/sqft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market), and the detached median was $1,365,000.

Roads and landmarks: Marine Way / Stewardson Way runs above the foreshore toward Burnaby; the Queensborough Bridge carries Highway 91A over the North Arm between the mainland and Queensborough; the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) is the foreshore trail.

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside North Arm; the nearest stations are 22nd Street Station (west) and New Westminster Station (north-east), both on the Expo Line, and TransLink route 100 (Marpole / 22nd Street Station) serves the Marine Way corridor above the foreshore.

Nearby areas: West End and Connaught Heights to the west above the foreshore, Downtown and the Quay to the north-east along the main-arm waterfront, Queensborough across the Queensborough Bridge to the south, and Burnaby across Marine Way to the west.

items.t: Flood / foreshore: the City floodplain study covers Fraser River land at the west end of the city in Floodplain Zone 2, and the North Arm is Fraser River foreshore — but the floodplain status of a specific North Arm lot is UNVERIFIED at lot level. Confirm the parcel's floodplain zone, any foreshore / water-lot tenure, and the insurance position before subject removal.

blocks.text: Good to know about North Arm

items.t: The same name means three different geographies. "North Arm" is (1) this board sub-area — the mainland New Westminster foreshore, with zero listings in September 2026; (2) a pair of City statistical / industrial areas, "North Arm North" and "North Arm South," not confirmed to match the board geography; and (3) a portal label applied to Queensborough / Port Royal and mainland-slope buildings that trade actively under other sub-areas. Any "North Arm average price" a portal generates is built from (3), not from this sub-area.

The river is the amenity and the paperwork. The sub-area's documented public asset is the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm), the foreshore trail named in the OCP Green Zone list — the same foreshore that puts floodplain, tenure and insurance checks at the front of any river-side purchase.
A zero month is the normal state here, not a market crash.
The recorded school sample does not belong to this sub-area.

No station, despite the corridor. Marine Way carries route 100 and through traffic above the foreshore, but the nearest SkyTrain stations are 22nd Street and New Westminster, both outside the sub-area — "SkyTrain-adjacent" is not a supportable description for a North Arm address.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in North Arm
Streets, schools and getting around North Arm

items.t: North Arm is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for New Westminster, named for the North Arm of the Fraser River: the river's north-arm foreshore along the south side of mainland New Westminster, below the Marine Way / Stewardson Way corridor, with the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) trail on the foreshore, named in the City's OCP Green Zone list. Precise boundary roads: UNVERIFIED. It is NOT one of the residential neighbourhoods on the City's Official Community Plan residential-neighbourhoods map, and its official City neighbourhood status is UNVERIFIED; the City's statistical planning geography separately uses "North Arm North" and "North Arm South" for industrial areas on the Queensborough / river side, and the board sub-area and the City statistical areas are not confirmed to be the same geography. Parks and Open Space.pdf

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere —. This is a foreshore / largely non-residential board geography, not a trading residential neighbourhood. The housing form the bylaw names for the slope above the foreshore is single detached housing.

Parent-community context only, cited exactly as the report states it, as "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED and never as a townhome-only figure: the New Westminster condos & townhomes median was $560,000 in September 2026 ($587/sqft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market), and the detached median was $1,365,000. New Westminster IS a SnapStats-covered community; North Arm's own sub-area rows are the zeros above.

Schools: School District 40 (New Westminster) runs a three-tier system — elementary K–5, middle 6–8, secondary 9–12 — and catchments are address-based. The master research recorded an SD40 locator run for the sample address 800 Queens Avenue (on the slope above the foreshore), returning École Qayqayt Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary — but that sample sits outside any confirmed North Arm boundary, so the catchment for an actual North Arm address is UNVERIFIED; check the exact address in the locator and never market the sample result as this sub-area's catchment.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in North Arm

items.t: Form B diligence (any strata purchase): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. There is no in-sub-area strata stock to apply this to today — it is the document that governs the Queensborough, Downtown, Quay and Connaught Heights purchases this search usually resolves to.

Fee-simple homes (the slope form): NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001) and any registered covenants or HOA documents only, stated plainly.

New Westminster property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026. The City also operates its own electrical utility alongside City water and sewer services.

blocks.text: Good to know about North Arm

items.t: The recorded school sample does not belong to this sub-area. The master research's SD40 locator run for 800 Queens Avenue (Fraser River Middle School's address, on the slope above the foreshore) returned Qayqayt / Fraser River / New Westminster Secondary — but that address sits outside any confirmed North Arm boundary, so the result must not be marketed as "the North Arm catchment."

New Westminster runs its own electric utility, alongside City water / sewer services — a running-cost setup unlike Richmond's or Burnaby's, and a genuine difference for a buyer comparing across the river. A 2026 utility dollar figure for a North Arm property: UNVERIFIED.

The Queensborough Bridge is the sub-area's hinge: it carries Highway 91A over the North Arm between the mainland and Queensborough, which is why Queensborough addresses — Mercer Village, Port Royal, Portside — surface in "North Arm" searches despite being a separate sub-area across the water.

blocks.text: Lots and land in North Arm
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Slope house parcels: houses on the slope above the foreshore sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 — the RS-1 district states a site of not less than 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio not over 0.5. That is the zone frame, not a claim about typical North Arm lot sizes: typical lot sizes are UNVERIFIED, and whether any given "North Arm" listing address is detached, strata or industrial is a parcel-by-parcel check.

Strata vs freehold: UNVERIFIED for this sub-area — zero listings in September 2026 gives no market split to report, and no official source read states the stock split. (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.)

Foreshore / water-lot position: foreshore and water-lot rules are provincial and are not confirmed for a specific lot in the research — foreshore tenure for any river-side parcel is UNCONFIRMED parcel-by-parcel and must be confirmed before subject removal. The OCP Green Zone includes the Esplanade (North Arm) and the Annacis Channel shoreline — trail/foreshore land, not lot stock. Parks and Open Space.pdf

Serviced position: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility and City water / sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a North Arm property confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED. Servicing for any single parcel is confirmed through the City's subdivision process under Bylaw No. 7142, 2007.
ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area was not confirmed in the sources read — no ALR split is stated, and ALR status for a specific property is checked in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Flood position: the City floodplain study covers Fraser River land at the west end of the city in Floodplain Zone 2, and the North Arm is Fraser River foreshore — but the floodplain status of a specific North Arm lot is UNVERIFIED at lot level.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around North Arm

items.t: It is NOT one of the residential neighbourhoods on the City's OCP residential-neighbourhoods map, and it is not listed as a separate City Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement — official City neighbourhood status: UNVERIFIED. The City's statistical planning geography does use "North Arm North" and "North Arm South" for the industrial areas on the Queensborough / river side; the board sub-area and the City statistical areas are not confirmed to be the same geography. Precise boundary roads: UNVERIFIED. Parks and Open Space.pdf

Main roads: Marine Way / Stewardson Way runs above the North Arm foreshore toward Burnaby and the Queensborough Bridge (Highway 91A), which crosses the North Arm of the Fraser River between the mainland and Queensborough. Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside North Arm; the nearest stations are 22nd Street Station (west) and New Westminster Station (north-east), both on the Expo Line; TransLink route 100 (Marpole / 22nd Street Station) serves the Marine Way corridor above the foreshore. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue (fully opened in May 2024; 10,644 sq. m., the City's largest capital project to date), is the city's main recreation centre, up the hill from the foreshore; the Main Branch of New Westminster Public Library is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown, with a kiosk and holds locker at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, in Downtown; Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton, is the city's hospital.
Schools: SD40 runs a three-tier system (elementary K–5, middle 6–8, secondary 9–12) and catchments are address-based.

Market context, labelled correctly: New Westminster IS a SnapStats-covered community, and SnapStats has NO land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: North Arm sub-area detached inventory 0 / solds 0 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 0 / 0 — no listings and no sales in either type; New Westminster community detached median $1,365,000 and condos & townhomes median $560,000. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only — and with zero sub-area sales there is no sub-area median to publish in any case).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in North Arm

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: slope houses sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) — RS-1: minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR not over 0.5.

OCP — "Our City 2041," Bylaw No. 7925, 2017: the area is governed by Our City 2041; the OCP Green Zone includes the Esplanade (North Arm) and the Annacis Channel shoreline. No North Arm area plan was confirmed on a City source.

Subdivision + servicing requirements — Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (VERIFIED): subdivision is regulated by the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007, which requires Approving Officer approval and ensures new lots are adequately serviced and meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements, through the City's pre-application / application / Works & Services Agreement process. Parcel-level standards are confirmed through that process; none is quoted here.

Foreshore + flood diligence: the City floodplain study covers west-end Fraser River land in Floodplain Zone 2 and the North Arm is Fraser River foreshore — confirm the parcel's floodplain zone, any foreshore / water-lot tenure, and the insurance position before subject removal. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying zones.

ALR rules (for completeness — no North Arm ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

blocks.text: Good to know about North Arm

items.t: The zero is the fact: a full month with zero listings and zero sales in both property types is itself the market information for this sub-area — any North Arm median, ratio or DOM figure offered by anyone is invented, because none can be computed from zero. (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.)

The bridge is the geography lesson: the Queensborough Bridge carries Highway 91A over the North Arm itself between the mainland and Queensborough — which is why Queensborough product keeps surfacing under North Arm portal labels, and why it still belongs in Queensborough's files.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: What is North Arm in New Westminster?
faq.a: On the board taxonomy it is a GVR MLS® sub-area named for the North Arm of the Fraser River — the river's northern branch and its foreshore along the south side of mainland New Westminster, carrying the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) trail named in the City's OCP Green Zone. The City does not list North Arm among its OCP residential neighbourhoods.

faq.q: What sold in North Arm in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing was listed or sold: 0 detached listings and 0 condos & townhomes listings, 0 solds in either type, so the sales ratio is not applicable and there is no sub-area median. At the New Westminster community level the detached median was $1,365,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $560,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station in North Arm?
faq.a: No; 22nd Street Station and New Westminster Station, both on the Expo Line, are the nearest, and TransLink route 100 serves the Marine Way corridor above the foreshore.

faq.q: Which bridge crosses the North Arm here?
faq.a: The Queensborough Bridge, carrying Highway 91A over the North Arm of the Fraser River between mainland New Westminster and Queensborough.

faq.q: Are there any condos for sale in North Arm?
faq.a: A portal showing "North Arm" condos is using its own North Arm North / North Arm South labels for Queensborough or mainland-slope buildings, which are different sub-areas.
This North Arm is the New Westminster foreshore on the river's north side.

faq.q: Are there any townhomes for sale in North Arm?
faq.a: A portal showing "North Arm" townhouses is using its own North Arm North / North Arm South labels for Queensborough or mainland-slope buildings, which are different sub-areas.

This North Arm is the New Westminster foreshore on the river's north side, and its stock files under New Westminster's Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 and OCP Bylaw No. 7925, 2017 — never Richmond's Zoning Bylaw 8500 / OCP 9000.

faq.q: Is Mercer Village a North Arm townhouse project?
faq.a: No. Mercer Village (388 Duncan Street) is a Queensborough townhome community by Plat:form + Domus — 146 townhomes on the presale source, with move-in-ready Freehold Strata units now listing — that happens to sit on the bank of the North Arm of the Fraser River. The river's name is not the board sub-area.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot or a home for sale in North Arm right now?
faq.a: Most homes a buyer means by this search actually sit in West End, Connaught Heights, Downtown, Quay or Queensborough — price from the actual sub-area. (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.)

faq.q: Can I quote a North Arm median or sales ratio?
faq.a: Use the New Westminster community figures only as labelled context (detached $1,365,000; condos & townhomes $560,000, September 2026). (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.)

faq.q: What zone frame governs a slope house above the foreshore?
faq.a: The RS districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 — RS-1 states a minimum site of 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and FSR not over 0.5 — and foreshore rules are provincial. Both are parcel-level confirmations.
